items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Michael Masser came to me... He said, 'I got this song I want you to hear... I'd like you to do it.' ... So we fought off everybody, and we created a classic.

ctx.x: Breezin’, In Flight, and then the Weekend in L.A.

Weekend in L.A., live. That’s where I told the story about my grandfather and my father meeting up for the first time in 21 years and, for me, 31 years. That was an exciting day. One quirk we had. On the first night, when we recorded On Broadway, I didn’t quite know where the tempo should be. So I was experimenting, and I started it off too slow. On the second set – if you hear the recording, you’ll hear me adjusting the tempo. It starts off real slow, then it speeds way up [Benson hums a phrase], and then I back…

So when we went for the playback – and I was happy with everything else – we got to what I believed was going to be the smash, because I never got a response on a song like that before, and then he played the first version on Friday night, which was the slow one. I said, “Tommy, take that off, man. That’s not the one.” He said, “George, this sounds fantastic. I’m telling you, this is” – I say, “Tommy, I’ve been listening to a version of this song that I know is going to be a smash.” He said, “I didn’t hear that.…
